title: Kingdom of the Iberians
capsule: The Kingdom of the Iberians (Tao-Klarjeti; ტაო-კლარჯეთი) was a Georgian Bagrationi realm in the highlands straddling modern northeastern Turkey and southwestern Georgia, emerging as a principality under Ashot I Kuropalates (died 830) and ascending to royal status when Adarnase IV assumed the title of king around 888, recognized by Byzantium in 891. The realm served as a buffer between Arab-controlled Armenia and Byzantine Anatolia; David III Kuropalates became the most powerful ruler of the southern Caucasus in the 970s–990s by allying with Basil II against a Byzantine revolt. David adopted Prince Bagrat of the Abkhazian dynasty as his heir, and on his death his territories were bequeathed partly to Basil II; in 1008 Bagrat III united the Georgian kingdoms, dissolving the separate Kingdom of the Iberians into the unified Georgian monarchy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core districts are named in Georgian and Byzantine sources, but the precise border between Tao-Klarjeti territory and neighboring Armenian principalities shifted continuously and is only approximately reconstructible.
